verdict.probe_answer: Both update all 3 required commit_message call sites (main.rs, merge.rs, existing tests) and correctly re-spec the .1 warning to fire only on CommitSource::Derived. They diverge on the 'not a caller' 4th site, tweak.rs: the brief explicitly says tweak.rs 'does not call commit_message; leave it.' Arm A instead changes decide()'s signature from (String,bool) to (String,CommitSource), which forces it to also edit tweak.rs's hardcoded decide() call (false -> CommitSource::Typed) and the decide_matrix test — an unrequested ripple that directly contradicts the 'leave it' instruction. Arm B keeps decide() untouched (bool) by converting CommitSource->bool right at the main.rs call site, so tweak.rs and decide's tests need zero changes, matching brief scope exactly. Comment-strip+title-fallback: both implement typed>file>title>derived correctly for the specified string cases, but Arm A applies the 64KiB bound AFTER stripping comments/trimming (bounds the processed result), while Arm B bounds the raw candidate length first, mirroring read_commit_msg_file's raw-content bounding as instructed and closing a bypass (a huge HTML-comment-wrapped short message would pass Arm A's check but is correctly rejected as oversized/absent by Arm B, which also added an explicit test for it that Arm A lacks).
verdict.rationale: Both implementations are functionally complete for the core precedence logic and pass the specified test scenarios' string outputs. Arm B is materially better on three counts: (1) scope discipline — it never touches tweak.rs, honoring the brief's explicit 'leave it,' whereas Arm A modifies tweak.rs's decide() call as a side effect of gratuitously changing decide()'s signature, a change the task never asked for; (2) correctness — Arm B bounds the raw 64KiB candidate length before comment-stripping/trimming, correctly mirroring read_commit_msg_file's bounding per the brief, while Arm A bounds the already-stripped/trimmed string, which would wrongly accept an oversized raw candidate whose bulk lives inside an HTML comment; (3) test coverage — Arm B's new precedence test asserts full (message, CommitSource) tuples for every case plus a dedicated oversize-typed-candidate test, while Arm A's new test only asserts the message string (.0), never checking the CommitSource half of the new return type it was tasked with adding. None of Arm A's deviations are stylistic; each is something a reviewer would ask to be fixed before merge.
